result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a wide, unmarked residential roadway with minimal infrastructure. A narrow sidewalk is present on one side but is partially obstructed by a large parked vehicle, and there are no marked crossings or traffic calming measures visible.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: A large white box truck parked on the left side of the street significantly blocks sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Left foreground, parked along the curb

hazards.name: Narrow/Inadequate Sidewalk
hazards.description: The sidewalk on the left is very narrow and lacks a buffer from the roadway, while the right side appears to lack a continuous paved walkway.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and right edges of the roadway

hazards.name: Wide Unmarked Roadway
hazards.description: The lack of lane markings and the width of the street may encourage higher vehicle speeds in a residential area without providing designated crossing points.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the image, spanning the width of the asphalt

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) at potential crossing points to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add high-visibility marked crosswalks to designate safe crossing locations for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening and Completion
interventions.description: Widen existing sidewalks to at least 5-6 feet and ensure a continuous paved network on both sides of the street.

result.summary: The image shows a residential corner with continuous sidewalks separated from the roadway by a grass buffer. However, the intersection lacks marked crosswalks and visible traffic control, and large corner bushes create a visual obstruction for pedestrians and drivers.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Large, dense bushes on the corner lot block sightlines between pedestrians waiting to cross and drivers approaching the intersection.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: The intersection lacks marked crosswalks, which reduces driver awareness of potential pedestrian activity.

hazards.name: Single Diagonal Curb Ramp
hazards.description: The single ramp at the corner apex directs pedestrians into the center of the intersection rather than across specific legs.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install high-visibility continental crosswalk markings to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Daylighting and Vegetation Management
interventions.description: Trim or remove corner vegetation to improve sightlines and ensure pedestrians are visible to turning motorists.

interventions.title: Directional Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Replace the single diagonal ramp with two separate ramps aligned with the crossing directions to improve accessibility and safety.

result.summary: The residential street features a sidewalk on one side with a grass buffer, but lacks a continuous walkway on the opposite side. The wide, unmarked roadway and absence of formal pedestrian crossings or traffic calming measures create an environment where vehicle speeds may be higher than appropriate for a neighborhood setting.

hazards.name: Missing Sidewalk
hazards.description: The right side of the street lacks a paved sidewalk, potentially forcing pedestrians to walk in the roadway.

hazards.name: Wide Unmarked Roadway
hazards.description: The lack of lane markings on a wide street can lead to higher vehicle speeds and unpredictable positioning.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Completion
interventions.description: Construct a continuous paved sidewalk on the right side of the street to provide a safe, separated space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install high-visibility marked crosswalks at the intersection to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming
interventions.description: Introduce speed humps or curb extensions to reduce vehicle speeds and shorten crossing distances.

result.summary: The image shows a quiet residential street with a continuous sidewalk separated from the roadway by a grass buffer. While the environment provides basic separation for pedestrians, it lacks formal infrastructure such as marked crossings, traffic calming, or visible street lighting.

hazards.name: Lack of street lighting
hazards.description: No street light poles are visible, which may reduce pedestrian safety and visibility during nighttime hours.

hazards.name: Wide unmarked roadway
hazards.description: The lack of lane markings on a relatively wide residential street can lead to higher vehicle speeds and unpredictable positioning.
